clue.text: Instrument, though not in red

indicators.note: says the instrument is taken without the following word, so those two letters drop out

parts.note: a clarinet is a woodwind instrument
the word in itself supplies the two letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone describes a musical instrument that, unusually, isn't painted red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not' removes IN from CLARINET. 'Red' looks like part of the instrument's description but is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is a deep purplish red, the colour named after Bordeaux red wine.

clue.text: Grouch mean, or miserable

indicators.note: something in a wretched state is out of order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A grumpy person is described as stingy or else unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miserable' rearranges the letters of MEAN OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouch is a habitual complainer, exactly someone who keeps grumbling and whining.

clue.text: Small bottle, one in private chamber brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
places the numeral inside the room's letters

parts.note: LAV is short for lavatory, a private little room
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A little bottle is carried upstairs, a single one being kept in a private room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside LAV to make LAIV, and 'brought up' reverses it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container for medicine or perfume, a little bottle.

clue.text: Fortune collected by seed in sport

indicators.note: the seed gathers the fortune up inside itself

parts.note: a pea is the seed of the pea plant
one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fortune from seed sold into the sports world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected by' means the seed holds the fortune, so the second word goes round the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelota is the Basque ball game played against a wall, a recognised sport.

clue.text: Cricketer bats, surprisingly, in red

indicators.note: places the jumbled letters inside the footballer's name

parts.note: Robbie Fowler was a striker for Liverpool, whose players are the Reds

indicators.note: a surprising turn of events reorders these letters

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cricketer in a red kit swings his bats to unexpected effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the letters of bats, and 'in' sets them inside the name. 'Red' looks like a kit colour but means a Liverpool player, Liverpool being the Reds.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast bowler is a cricketer who bowls at high pace, a kind of player rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Redpoll in red, good for bird

indicators.note: places that initial inside the communist's name

parts.note: a Red is a communist, and Stalin led the Soviet communists
read as Red's poll: a poll is an old word for a head, and the head of Red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports a redpoll in red plumage, which is good news for the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redpoll' looks like the finch but splits into Red's poll, its head R. 'in' puts it inside STALIN, 'red' being a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird found across Britain and much of the world.

clue.text: Turn on leader of establishment overwhelmed by sarcastic jokes

indicators.note: the outer word swamps and surrounds the inner letters

parts.note: dry humour is ironic and sarcastic

indicators.note: in a down clue the turning word sits on top of the following letter

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone turns on a figure from the establishment who is swamped by mocking jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works because this is a down clue: the turning word sits above the leader. 'overwhelmed by' means the sarcastic word surrounds both.
explanation.definitionFit: Drollery is comic, whimsical humour, a collective name for amusing jests.

clue.text: Papal order initially in red reaching troublesome conclusion

indicators.note: puts that letter inside the communist leader's name

parts.note: a Red is a communist, and Lenin was the founding Bolshevik leader

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word it follows
the conclusion of the word troublesome is its final letter

explanation.surface: A papal command, at first dressed in red, comes to an awkward end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives O, which 'in' places inside LENIN; then add E, the last letter of 'troublesome'. 'Red' means a communist here.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine can mean relating to one of the popes named Leo, hence papal in that narrow sense.

clue.text: Peacock feathers finally put in hat

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the hat

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped straw hat

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Peacock feathers are, in the end, stuck into someone's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives S, the last letter of feathers; 'put in' places it inside BOATER. 'Peacock' is the show-off, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A peacock is figuratively a vain show-off, someone who brags about himself.

clue.text: Grey in red, most striking

indicators.note: places the word for aged inside the player's name

parts.note: George Best played for Manchester United, nicknamed the Red Devils
grey hair suggests being old

explanation.surface: Grey set against red makes the most eye-catching colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the insertion. 'Grey' and 'red' look like a colour scheme, but 'red' is George Best of Manchester United, the Red Devils.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldest is the superlative of bold, describing something vivid and eye-catching in the highest degree.

clue.text: Red ball frayed either side: movement around that

indicators.note: the musical movement goes round the frayed letters

parts.note: a rondo is a piece or movement with a recurring theme

indicators.note: a word worn away at both edges loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A red ball, worn at both ends, has something moving around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frayed either side' and 'around that' are the indicators. 'Red' is the definition, not the ball's colour: Cristiano Ronaldo played for Manchester United, the Red Devils.
explanation.definitionFit: Cristiano Ronaldo played for Manchester United, whose players are called the Reds.

clue.text: Side at a future date meeting Arsenal wingers

parts.note: later means at some time afterwards

indicators.note: a team's wingers play on the outside, so the word's outer letters are taken

explanation.surface: A team arranges a fixture at a future date against Arsenal's wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' gives A and L, the outside letters of Arsenal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral means relating to the side, as in a lateral pass or lateral view.

clue.text: Stop bullying entire team drained of energy

indicators.note: bullying knocks things about, so the letters are pushed into a new order
the fodder is emptied of one letter

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A coach demands an end to the bullying that has left the whole team exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained of' removes one E from ENTIRE TEAM, and 'bullying' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate something is to bring it to an end, to halt it.

clue.text: Feeling nothing new in intestine after treatment

indicators.note: puts the letter inside the rearranged word
treatment processes and reshapes the word, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A patient feels nothing new in the gut after undergoing treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after treatment' rearranges INTESTINE, and 'in' places N among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insentient means lacking sensation or consciousness, so incapable of feeling anything.

clue.text: Green wire attached to complete circuit?

indicators.note: the wire is joined onto the end of the ring

parts.note: the letter O is a complete ring, a full circuit
a live wire is a wire carrying current

explanation.surface: An electrician connects a green wire to finish off a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' and 'wire' suggest the earth cable in British wiring, but 'Green' is the definition and the circuit is just the shape O.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a dull yellowish-green shade, named after the unripe fruit.

clue.text: Puzzle on something red in London

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
London's double-decker buses are famously red

explanation.surface: A puzzle is set about some red thing found in London.
explanation.walkthrough: London's public buses are painted red, so a bus is a red thing in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a picture puzzle where images and letters stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Plant most of bed so comes up in red

indicators.note: puts the reversed letters inside the player's name

parts.note: Ian Rush was a Liverpool striker, Liverpool being the Reds

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up reads the letters from bottom to top
most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener plants most of a bed so that it comes up red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the bed, 'comes up' reverses that with so in this down clue, giving OSEB, and 'in' places it inside a Liverpool striker's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosebush is a shrub that bears roses, a particular garden plant.

clue.text: Scoring marks, 51 in red

indicators.note: places the numeral inside the player's name

parts.note: John Barnes played on the wing for Liverpool, the Reds
LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A tally of scoring marks shows fifty-one in red ink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the insertion. 'Scoring' refers to musical scores, not goals, and 'red' is a Liverpool winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar lines are the vertical lines dividing a musical score into bars, marks in written music.

clue.text: Half behind machine

indicators.note: takes the first half of the word for one's rear

parts.note: a behind is the bottom or buttocks

explanation.surface: Someone is half lagging behind a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes the first half of BOTTOM, the backside sense of 'behind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bot is a robot, or a program running automatically, so an automated machine.

clue.text: Red meat at bottom of stream

indicators.note: in a down clue the meat sits beneath the stream's letters

parts.note: a beck is a brook, a northern English word for a stream
ham is cured pork, a meat

explanation.surface: Some red meat is found lying at the bottom of a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a description of the meat, but it defines David Beckham, the Manchester United (Red Devils) midfielder.
explanation.definitionFit: David Beckham came through and starred at Manchester United, whose players are the Reds.

clue.text: Tall sunflower in the middle, yellow perhaps?

indicators.note: takes the centre letter of the nine-letter flower name

parts.note: eggy means like egg, and yolk-yellow is one example of that

explanation.surface: A tall sunflower, perhaps yellow in its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle' picks L, the fifth of SUNFLOWER's nine letters. 'perhaps' warns that yellow is only an example of eggy colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Leggy means having long legs, so lanky and tall in build.

clue.text: Charmer backing winner, I seethe somewhat

indicators.note: the found letters run backwards through the text
only a part of the words is used, so letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A gambler backs a winner while someone else quietly fumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes NERIS from within 'winner, I seethe', and 'backing' reverses it. 'backing winner' reads like betting.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the Sirens lured sailors with song, so a siren is a seductive charmer.

clue.text: Actors considered fixed

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a production
to rate something is to consider or judge it

explanation.surface: Actors were thought to have been bribed into rigging something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' looks like 'rigged', but it is the vet's sense, as when a pet is neutered.
explanation.definitionFit: To have an animal fixed is a euphemism for neutering it, which for a male means gelding.

clue.text: Extra flash

definitions.meaning: additional, as a further helping or a backup copy
an instant, as in 'back in a flash'

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a further helping is a second one, and a very brief moment is a second.

clue.text: On top, solver's blessed with outstanding dining equipment?

parts.note: on top means in addition, also
thy is the old word for your, and the clue addresses the solver as you

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that, on top of everything, the solver owns impressive cutlery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'dining equipment' is a set of teeth, and 'outstanding' means sticking out; the question mark flags this playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothy describes someone with large or prominent teeth, the mouth's own eating tools.

clue.text: Explain when bit of fish found in river

indicators.note: the fish part is placed within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a fin is one part of a fish

explanation.surface: Someone asks how part of a fish came to be in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' marks the insertion; 'when' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To define a term is to state its meaning precisely, so to make it clear.

clue.text: Berlin regularly leading this silly race

indicators.note: the picked letters come in front
takes every other letter of the city's name
silly suggests the letters are mixed about foolishly

explanation.surface: A Berlin runner regularly leads this silly race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes B, R, I from Berlin; 'silly' rearranges THIS to TISH. 'race' means a people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Race here means a people or nation, and the British form one such people.

clue.text: Stop upper chamber briefly going in a little lower

indicators.note: the shortened room goes inside the young animal

parts.note: a cow lows, so a small one is a calf

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a loft is a room up under the roof

explanation.surface: A legislator calls to stop the upper chamber briefly going in a lower house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upper chamber' and 'lower' suggest parliament; a 'lower' is really a cow, from the verb to low. 'briefly' cuts a letter and 'going in' marks the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To call off an event is to cancel it, bringing it to a stop.

clue.text: Green area, red and green ultimately

parts.note: Denis Law played for Manchester United, nicknamed the Red Devils

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A green patch is described as red and green in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives N, the last letter of green. 'red' is the Manchester United forward Denis Law.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is an expanse of mown grass, a green patch of ground.

clue.text: Bone in grave: I'm not sure

parts.note: stern and grave both mean serious and severe
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a bone found in a grave, uncertain what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' wants to be a burial place; it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the breastbone, the flat bone at the front of the ribcage.

clue.text: Ending in detention, the short red skirts bringing expression of mild reproof

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the following word
the player's name goes around the edges of the shortened word

parts.note: Michael Owen was a Liverpool striker, Liverpool being the Reds

indicators.note: the word is cut by its last letter

explanation.surface: Detention ends, and the short red skirts provoke a teacher's mild telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like clothing but is the verb, going round; 'short' cuts the last letter of 'the', and 'Ending in' takes a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Now then' is a mild warning, the sort said to calm or gently scold someone.
